summary: Live Cursor capture demonstrated end to end. Project-level .cursor/hooks.json in an owned scratch repo (branch feature/a07-live-demo) plus a real logged-in 'cursor-agent -p --output-format stream-json' run. Hook spool (B05), cursor-cli stream (B10), agent transcript (B07) and a backup copy of ai-code-tracking.db (B06) were collected through the real collectors into a real SQLite store, attributed to the branch, analyzed and explained. Source-reported tokens reach the per-branch report. The A07 composition/CLI wiring was not done because A02 holds the integration baton.

gaps: No built-CLI e2e yet (dx collect/analyze through apps/cli/dist/cli.js), because CLI wiring belongs to A02. The test drives the same handlers (runCollect, runAnalyze, runExplain) and the real collectors in-process.

No built hook entrypoint in the repo. The live demo used a scratch hook.mjs that calls handleCursorHook from a scratch tsc build. A02/C13 must ship a 'dx hook cursor' command (runCursorHook) and register it in the project .cursor/hooks.json.
Money: cursor-agent CLI, hooks, transcripts and ai-code-tracking.db report no charge, so charge stays unavailable. Cost needs a usage CSV (B08) or the SDK (B44).
cursor-agent does not report reasoning tokens, so they stay unavailable.
Stop hooks in this run carried no usage. Per-request tokens come only from a saved cursor-agent stream-json output.
ai-code-tracking.db is global, not repo-scoped. Its 8 ai.tool-edit rows got the collect-context branch, which is correct only when collected for the active repo and time window.
In the live run dx.git.commits=0 because the agent's edits were not committed (uncommitted-files=1). The fixture test commits and asserts commits=1.
The B05/B10/B07 descriptors still carry 'live-capture-not-demonstrated'. Their owners can now remove it, citing this run.
